stem: A facility uses RF adjunct technology plus manual sponge counts. At the end of an abdominal procedure, the manual closing count is correct but RF verification is not yet done. The surgeon asks to complete wound closure. What should the circulating nurse do?

options.A: Allow closure because a correct manual count makes RF verification unnecessary
options.B: Complete the required RF verification before final wound closure and communicate any discrepancy
options.C: Skip RF verification if the scrub person and surgeon verbally confirm the count
options.D: Allow closure and perform RF verification after the client leaves the OR

rationale: Manual counts can be falsely reassuring. AORN recommends adjunct technology as a supplement when used and directs completion of the manual count and adjunct verification before wound closure according to manufacturer instructions and facility policy. Verbal agreement does not replace the established verification process, and post-closure verification is too late for its prevention purpose.
educational_objective: When adjunct technology is part of the facility RSI-prevention process, complete it before wound closure even when the manual count is correct.
source_document_title: Using Adjunct Technology with the Surgical Count
source_locator: Considerations for Using Adjunct Technology — follow IFU/facility policy; use adjunct technology even when manual count is correct; complete manual count and adjunct technology before wound closure
source_claim_supported: AORN supports adjunct technology as a supplement to manual counting and states to complete both before wound closure when adjunct technology is used.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Safe Use of Equipment / client safety activities, printed pp.24-26
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — procedural safety and safe technology use
correction_summary: Rebuilt purpose-of-counting trivia into an RSI near-miss decision and made facility RF use explicit to avoid a universal technology claim.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Current AORN RSI resources and explicit adjunct-technology pre-closure guidance verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Manual-count fallibility and pre-closure adjunct use are supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect: manual count can be falsely reassuring.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect: verbal confirmation does not replace required verification.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Facility RF use is explicit, leaving B uniquely best.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are realistic OR actions.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Facility-policy dependence, universalization and alternate answers rechecked; no unresolved conflict.
